messages:
sara_support: Hey — customer AcmeHealth reports p95/p99 spikes for Dedicated pool during their daily billing-run window (approx 00:00-00:20 UTC). They see p99 ~6s vs baseline 800ms. Happening for the past 3 days. Anyone seen related autoscale issues? :worried:

mike_sre: saw similar alerts last night, graphs show scale-up attach lag spiking. p99 attach latency up to 35-45s in the same window. Possible thundering attach to a drained pool?

anita_eng: can you paste the sample request ids and models? might be model warmup heavy (long context, kv init).

sara_support: request ids: req_2026-03-15_2338_az, req_2026-03-16_0005_bk (I pasted the logs to the ticket). Model: rwd-70b-int8 + routing -> dedicated-pool-42.

ken_platform: looking at pool-42 metrics: spike in provisioning queue and attach retries around 00:02 UTC. autoscaler triggered new nodes but heartbeats delayed from provisioner (~20s). Attach backoff caused client retries -> longer tail.

ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool-42 attach_fail_rate increased by 8x at 2026-03-16T00:01:43Z. Instance warmup time median increased from 6s->28s.

mike_sre: likely two contributing things: 1) cold GPU image pulls during window (registry rate limits), 2) busy kernel compile on first attach (rwd-70b int8). Both add ~15-30s. Add attach retries -> p99 balloon.

laura_support: customer says it only affects their Dedicated capacity and is correlated with their high batch during billing. They need a short-term mitigation while engineering investigates.

anita_eng: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) enable proactive warmup for pool-42 min_pool to keep N extra warm workers, 2) fallback routing: route to hosted rwd-13b or quantized variant on attach failures, 3) reduce client retry/backoff so we don't amplify attach storm. Which is lowest-risk?

ken_platform: lowest-risk = fallback route to hosted 13b (config change in routing policy). We can also set min_pool +=2 for pool-42 for the billing window (manual override) — will raise cost but buys latency. I'll prepare a config change.

mike_sre: also flip kernel-image prefetch on next deploy for pool-42 region; that'll reduce compile time for first attach. Ops: how fast can you do min_pool change?

ken_platform: I can push a manual min_pool override within 10 minutes. Will monitor attach latency and p99.

laura_support: I'll update the customer with ETA: proactive warmup + temporary fallback to hosted 13b. Also ask them to throttle burst into reserved queue if possible.

ops-bot: [runbook link] autoscale-attach-lag-debugging — recommends increasing min_pool, enabling prewarm, and adding fallback rules.

anita_eng: medium-term: engineering to look at image pull parallelism, reduce registry throttling, and build lightweight standby kernel images for int8 variants so coldstart <5s. I'll file an action item.

mike_sre: action items I/O: 1) ken to apply min_pool override + routing fallback (in flight), 2) anita to open infra ticket for image prefetch & kernel-standby, 3) laura to update customer and confirm impact. I will watch SLO dashboards and check attach telemetry.

sara_support: thanks team. I'll add the customer-facing note: "We enabled warm workers and fallback to hosted 13B during your nightly billing window; we are monitoring — please ping if you still see >2s p95."

ken_platform: done — min_pool +2 applied to pool-42 for 00:00-00:30 UTC daily, routing fallback added to policy. Monitoring: current p99 reduced to ~1.1s on test traffic.

mike_sre: verified from telemetry: attach latency tail improved, p99 trending down. leaving a 6h watch window.

laura_support: customer update sent, they acknowledged and asked for a postmortem once root cause fixed.

anita_eng: ticket filed: INFRA-4321 "image pull & kernel warmup improvements for int8 models". Estimated triage in next sprint.

sara_support: closing loop for now. If p99 recurs during next billing run, re-open and we'll escalate. Thanks everyone :heart:
